name: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
notes: SPARSE/DENSE AMBIGUITY IN NVIDIA'S OWN TABLE: neither the datasheet nor the product page labels the Tensor Core figures as sparse or dense, and the datasheet itself only prints FP4 ('Peak FP4 AI PFLOPS 4 PFLOPS'); FP8/FP16/BF16/TF32 appear only on the product page. Cross-checking against NVIDIA's RTX PRO Blackwell architecture whitepaper (Table 4, which gives dense/sparse pairs for the same GB202 die at a 2617 MHz Workstation clock) scaled to this card's 2430 MHz boost clock (product brief) gives: TF32 dense 234 / sparse 468, FP16 dense 468 / sparse 936, FP8 dense 936 / sparse 1871, FP4 dense 1871 / sparse 3742. So the published FP4 (4 PFLOPS), FP8 (2 PFLOPS) and FP16/BF16 (1 PFLOP) figures are rounded-up SPARSE values and are recorded in the *_sparse fields as published, while the published TF32 figure (234) matches the DENSE value and is recorded in tf32_tensor_tflops. NVIDIA's table therefore appears to mix conventions across rows; the published values are kept verbatim (not replaced by the arithmetic above) and dense counterparts are left null rather than derived. Third-party sites disagree on how to read these figures (some label all of them dense, some all sparse) -- neither is supported by the whitepaper arithmetic. fp32_tflops of 120 is as published; 24,064 cores x 2 x 2430 MHz computes to ~117 TFLOPS (NVIDIA rounds up). fp64 not published for this card; NVIDIA's whitepaper states GB202 runs FP64 at 1/64 the FP32 rate (~1.9 TFLOPS here), so it is not an FP64 card -- left null as not published. INT8 and FP6 Tensor Core throughput are not published for the Server Edition (the whitepaper lists INT8 for the Workstation Edition only) -- left null. gpu_chip GB202 and sm_count 188 are taken from NVIDIA's whitepaper for the RTX PRO 6000 Workstation Edition, which has identical CUDA (24,064), Tensor (752) and RT (188) core counts; NVIDIA's Server Edition documents do not name the die. process_node_nm 4 = TSMC '4N' (NVIDIA custom), a marketing node name per the same whitepaper. NVLink explicitly 'Not supported' (product brief). slot_width 2 / cooling_type 'air' describe the standard dual-slot FHFL passively-cooled PCIe card; NVIDIA's product page also lists a liquid-cooled single-slot FHXL variant, not modeled as a separate record. tdp_watts_max 600 is the default/max in the 600 W strapping mode (a 450 W mode also exists; 300 W minimum). pcie_bandwidth_gbps 128 is the PCIe 5.0 x16 figure NVIDIA quotes for Gen5 on its Hopper datasheets; it is not stated in this card's own documents. This is the part AWS lists as 'RTX PRO Server 6000' in EC2 G7e instance metadata. NVIDIA announced it 2025-03-18 at GTC (press release); partner platforms from May 2025.
